title: Toys & Hobbies Ecommerce Benchmarks in 2026
summary: Conversion rate, AOV and bounce rate benchmarks for the Toys and Hobbies ecommerce category in 2026.
body_markdown:
## **Still Fourth in Conversion — With Basket Sizes Trailing Last Year**


The benchmarks:[2.03% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$329 median AOV.](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) Toys & Hobbies ranks fourth in CVR across the 10 published industries — the highest of the bottom seven categories and above the cross-industry median of 1.74%.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Toys & Hobbies.


Conversion fell 16.5% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters. That figure needs two caveats. First, the matched group is just 13 stores, tied with Consumer Electronics for the smallest in this benchmark series, so a handful of stores can move it significantly. Second, Q3 is a weak stretch for this category: over the same quarters in 2025, CVR fell 42.5%. The direction is probably real — Q3 was soft — but it was less soft than the year before.


AOV tells a steadier story within the year, and a weaker one against last year. The year-to-date median is $329, and same-store AOV slipped 2.5% from Q2 to Q3 ($314 to $306). Year over year, matched AOV is down 4.0% — the largest decline of the nine categories we report on that measure.


> Toys & Hobbies still ranks fourth in CVR at 2.03% — meaningful for a category often associated with considered, gift-oriented purchases. The pressure is on basket size: it has the weakest year-over-year AOV trend of any reported category, at −4.0%.


## Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date


The median Toys & Hobbies CVR from January through September 2026 was 2.03%, fourth among the 10 published industries.


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Toys & Hobbies cohort: n=15. Small cohort sizes increase the influence of individual stores on the median. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


A 2.03% median CVR places Toys & Hobbies in the upper half of the dataset, separated from the repeat-purchase leaders (Health & Wellness, Beauty, Food & Beverage) but above the considered-purchase categories. The P25-to-P75 range is 0.48%–3.28%, a 6.8× spread — the widest in the dataset, suggesting real variation in performance across the cohort.


The relatively high CVR for a gift-oriented category may reflect a few things. Toys and hobby products often have clear gift appeal, which can drive decisive purchases. Hobby enthusiasts — collectors, model builders, gamers — also tend to know exactly what they want before they arrive at a product page, which shortens the session-to-checkout path. These are possible contributing factors, not confirmed explanations.


> At 2.03% median CVR with a P75 of 3.28%, Toys & Hobbies outperforms the cross-industry median by 29 basis points. If your store is in this category and converting below 0.48%, you’re in the bottom quartile — a meaningful gap from where most peers are landing.


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Toys & Hobbies stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network.


n=11–18 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. With cohort sizes this small, individual months can move materially on the addition or removal of a single store — directional trends are more reliable than specific monthly figures. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Toys & Hobbies.


The 21-month CVR data shows a category with pronounced peaks around the holidays. November 2025 (2.45%) and December 2025 (2.22%) are the two highest months in the window, and July 2025 (2.03%) also stands out above the surrounding months. The category appears to convert at higher rates during certain periods — whether driven by gifting occasions, promotional activity, or the timing of product launches is hard to isolate from aggregate data.


2026 has run softer. Monthly CVR has stayed between 0.85% and 1.56% all year, and Q3 came in at 0.92% in July, 1.30% in August and 1.02% in September. The year-to-date aggregate of 2.03% (from the CVR report’s period cohort) is higher than any individual 2026 month, because the period calculation weights each store’s full nine-month performance differently than a monthly median does — and with only 11–14 stores a month in 2026, single months move on very little data.


Bounce rates remain the steadiest in this benchmark series, with the lowest month-to-month variation of any category. The 21-month range is 32.1%–42.4%, with most months between 33% and 38%. The Q2 uptick (42.4% in May, 41.5% in June) eased in Q3, with July through September holding near 37%.


> Toys & Hobbies has the steadiest bounce rate trend in the dataset across 21 months. While CVR moved around considerably month to month, bounce rates barely shifted — suggesting that traffic quality remained fairly consistent even as conversion outcomes varied.


## **Average Order Value Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Toys & Hobbies was $329. This data covers full-store Shopify order data, separate from the CVR cohort above.


January–September 2026, n=70 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Toys & Hobbies.


## **AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below tracks monthly median AOV for Toys & Hobbies stores, with each month measured on its own (53–74 stores per month).


n=53–74 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Toys & Hobbies.


The AOV trend is far more volatile than the bounce rate trend. The 16-month range runs from $259 (May 2026) to $387 (July 2025) — a $128 spread. With 53–74 stores a month, individual months can move on a small number of merchants.


The pattern has a seasonal shape. Summer 2025 ran high ($362–$387 from June through August), fell in September and October ($305 and $285), then jumped back to $383 in November before easing to $346 in December — consistent with a holiday lift in gift and hobby spending, though the data can’t confirm the cause.


2026 has run lower than the same months of 2025. Most months landed between $259 and $307, with July ($332) the exception. August ($280) and September ($286) came in below August and September 2025 ($378 and $305), and same-store AOV slipped 2.5% from Q2 to Q3.


On a matched same-store basis (n=51 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV moved from $384 to $368 — a −4.0% year-over-year decline, the largest of the nine categories we report on this measure. The direction is consistent with the softer AOV trend visible in the monthly data.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


On the AOV side, Toys & Hobbies looks soft but orderly. Order values eased slightly from Q2 to Q3 (−2.5%) and sit 4.0% below last year among stores active in both periods. The monthly data shows where the gap sits: 2026 has run below a strong mid-2025.


CVR is more variable, and the small cohort (15 stores in the period snapshot, 13 in the matched Q2→Q3 cohort) amplifies that variability. The −16.5% Q2→Q3 decline is milder than the category’s −42.5% move over the same months of 2025, but with 13 matched stores, the confidence interval around either figure is wide. The directional signal — Q3 was a weak quarter, as it was last year — is probably real. The specific numbers should be read loosely.


> The Toys & Hobbies benchmarks come with a meaningful small-sample caveat throughout. The CVR cohort is 15 stores — the smallest in the dataset and right at our publishing minimum. The AOV cohort (70 stores) is more robust. Treat the CVR figures as directional guides rather than precise targets.


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Toys & Hobbies**


The P25-to-P75 AOV range of $167–$697 covers a 4.2× spread — wider than most categories in the dataset. That range reflects how different the underlying businesses can be. A merchant selling trading cards or small hobby accessories sits at a very different price point than one selling model kits, musical instruments, or high-end hobby equipment.


CVR likely varies just as much by sub-market. A store selling low-cost, impulse-friendly products may convert at rates well above 3.28% (the P75). A store selling $500+ hobby equipment — RC vehicles, scale models, professional art supplies — may convert closer to the P25 or below. The 2.03% median captures the middle of a wide distribution.


For merchants in this category, the most useful benchmark comparison is within your own sub-market rather than against the category headline. If you know your AOV sits near the P75 ($697), compare your CVR against considered-purchase categories. If your AOV is closer to $150–$200, the repeat-purchase category benchmarks may be more instructive.


> The $329 median AOV and 2.03% CVR are the right starting points for Toys & Hobbies benchmarking — but with a 4.2× AOV spread and only 15 stores in the CVR cohort, the sub-market you’re in likely matters more than the category aggregate.
